title: Release-train radar and OKRs-to-capacity map
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a lightweight, stakeholder-friendly 'release-train radar' visualization and an OKRs-to-capacity mapping layer that surfaces where planned initiatives map to available runway and reserve capacity across runtime/console/API release lanes. The goal is to give PMs, Eng leads, and GTM stakeholders a single pane to: (1) prioritize which initiatives must ride the next train, (2) visualize OKR alignment and risk exposure by lane, and (3) produce automated capacity hedging suggestions (buffer, canary windows, regional gating). This is an orchestration and planning feature (not enforcement) intended to reduce coordination friction, shorten pre-launch negotiations, and tie launch commitments directly to OKRs and committed GPU capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive radar that displays initiatives by objective alignment, planned start date, and estimated GPU-hours (or FTE-equivalent) per lane.
Ability for PM to assign OKR tags to initiatives and for the map to aggregate OKR-level 'demand' vs. lane 'supply'.
A capacity hedging suggestion engine that recommends: buffer % by lane, preferred canary window, and fallback model variant when capacity delta > threshold.
Exportable CSV/JSON of lane allocation and suggested hedges for use by Eng capacity planning and finance forecasting.
Basic permissions: PMs can edit initiative metadata; Eng leads can override capacity estimates; audit log entries for final cut decisions.
Dashboard link from Console launch calendar; must render correctly for teams with >200 initiatives in view (performance test).

updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting. Alignment on desired inputs: initiative_id, okr_tags, estimated_gpu_hours, lane_preference, hard_deadline, owner. Action: ENG to surface capacity telemetry; Design to explore compact radar UI for Console.

2026-03-05: Data model spec posted to Confluence. Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/Release-Train-Radar-Data-Model. Request for Eng: add 'estimated_gpu_hours' to initiative API by Mar 12.

2026-03-09: Design mockups reviewed. Feedback: needs clearer visual encoding for 'hedge suggested' vs 'soft buffer'. Decided to use a three-band radial ring (Committed / Buffer / Risk) to reduce label clutter.

2026-03-10: Engineering feasibility sync. Trade-offs discussed: real-time capacity pulls vs cached daily snapshot. Decision: start with daily snapshot to reduce runtime load; plan real-time toggle for Q3 if adoption warrants.

2026-03-11: Prototype PR opened for export API: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1247. Backend owner: @jamie-park. Notes: export includes initiative metadata and computed hedges; requires infra flag 'radar-export'.

2026-03-12: Stakeholder review with Runtime leads. Request: add an auto-fallback policy mapping when recommended buffer > 30% (suggest specific quantized model variant). Action: PM to add mapping table to spec.

2026-03-12: Risk flagged: current initiative estimates in product tracker are inconsistent. Mitigation: Eng leads will run a 48-hour calibration pass on estimates and surface corrections in the export CSV. Assigned to: Ravi Singh.
risks: Estimate quality - initiative owners under/over estimate GPU-hours leading to misleading hedges.
Over-automation - teams might treat suggested hedges as enforced gates; must be careful with terminology and UI affordances.
Performance - rendering many initiatives in the radar could exceed client-side limits; will implement server-side aggregation for large result sets.
Data freshness - daily snapshot means short-term spikes may not be visible; docs must call this out and show alternate real-time metrics in Console.
decisions: Start with daily capacity snapshot instead of real-time pulls to minimize backend cost and unblock fast delivery.
Use three-band radial visualization (Committed / Buffer / Risk) to communicate hedges compactly.
Expose suggestions as 'recommended' actions; do not implement automatic enforcement in this launch. Enforcement is a follow-up after adoption.
Integrate with existing launch calendar deep links rather than building a separate scheduling surface to reduce context switching.
